..
A minor trade-wind trough brought isolated showers to the region
today. Tonight, a stronger trade-wind trough extending from an active
segment of the Near-Equatorial Trough (NET) to the south is expected
to bring scattered showers to the region with slightly higher 
chances for Guam and Rota. Upper-level divergence paired with
relatively dry mid-level air may give way to a few thunderstorms, 
but will mainly be concentrated over the southern half of the 
Marianas. Lingering scattered showers will continue for Guam and Rota
Friday before clearing out and returning to 20 percent chances of
showers throughout the rest of the forecast period. The zones were
split due to the short-term forecast differences, so they may be
combined again over the next few updates.

Marine...
Combined seas of 5 to 7 feet may increase to 6 to 8 feet by the end
of the weekend. A trade swell continues to dominate the region. There
is a moderate risk of rip currents along east-facing reefs at least 
through Friday night. There may be isolated sets reaching 8 feet 
along east-facing reefs, but overall surf is likely within the lower 
end of the 6 to 8 foot range based on today's surf observations.

Fire weather...
If rainfall can exceed 0.20 inches from the trade-wind trough 
expected tonight and Friday, the Keech-Bryam Drought Index (KBDI) may
temporarily halt its upward trend. Based on current model guidance, 
however, that is unlikely. Isolated showers returning this weekend 
in addition to moderate to fresh trades will continue the KBDI climb.
Folks are urged to monitor any outdoor-related activities that 
involve a spark or flames, as elevated conditions are ongoing.

Eastern Micronesia...
The Near-Equatorial Trough (NET) remains active today, as it
stretches east-southeast from south of Chuuk to east-southeast of
Kosrae, before turning east. The best surface convergence is observed
along and just north of this boundary, which favors Kosrae having the
best rainfall coverage/potential, followed by Majuro. As such, look
for periods of scattered showers (locally numerous at Kosrae) and
isolated thunderstorms through the weekend, with Majuro being too 
far north/removed from the convergence to see anything more than 
isolated showers. 

Then, the NET will pivot some, giving Pohnpei a period of drier
weather early next week, while Kosrae continues to see scattered
showers, while rainfall coverage/potential increases at Majuro, as
this portion of the NET lifts north and acts as a focus for 
convective development.

As for marine conditions, mariners can generally expect to see
moderate to fresh conditions much of the period area-wide. Seas of 5
to 7 feet may build a foot towards the weekend and into next week, as
the pressure gradient tightens between the NET and high pressure to
the north, allowing sea heights to increase somewhat. Surf will
remain elevated for north-facing reefs at Pohnpei, and north and
east-facing reefs at Kosrae, the next several days due as surf is
augmented by the trade swell.

Western Micronesia...
A wet and unsettled weather pattern will continue at Palau and 
Chuuk. The pattern is produced by the NET. Scattered to widespread 
showers are expected through at least the beginning of next week. Up
to an inch of daily rainfall is possible while the NET remains in 
the region. Trade winds of 15 to 20 mph (10 to 15 kt) are expected, 
with occasional gusts to 30 mph (25 kt) possible. Overall, wet and 
near breezy conditions are to be expected for the next several days 
at Palau and Chuuk.

Yap is expected to remain on the northern extent of the NET. Showers
are expected to build in for the weekend. Like the showers over the
rest of the region, up to an inch rainfall is to be expected. Model 
guidance suggest drier conditions will return around the beginning of
the work week. 

This would be a great opportunity to catch rain and top off water 
reserves for all three locations. 

Combined seas of 5 to 7 feet are seen across the region. Seas are 
forecast to maintain the 5 to 7 foot range through the beginning of
next week. This will keep surf around 7 to 8 feet along north- and 
east-facing reefs. Seas and surf are expected to remain below 
advisory thresholds of 10 foot seas and 9 foot surf. Light to 
moderate winds are expected throughout the coastal regions. Winds 
will gradually taper down for the beginning of next week.
